query_text: Does it matter what we eat?

content.text:
Yes — **what we eat matters a lot**, though it doesn’t have to be complicated or perfect.

Food affects:

- **Energy and mood:** meals with enough protein, fiber, and healthy fats tend to keep blood sugar steadier.
- **Long-term health:** eating patterns rich in vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, and minimally processed foods are linked with lower risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and some cancers.
- **Body weight and appetite:** highly processed, sugary, and low-fiber foods can make it easier to overeat.
- **Gut health:** fiber-rich foods feed beneficial gut bacteria.
- **Brain function:** hydration, micronutrients, and overall diet quality can affect concentration and mental health.
- **Performance and recovery:** protein, carbohydrates, and micronutrients matter for physical activity and healing.

A simple rule of thumb: **most of the time, build meals around plants, protein, fiber-rich carbs, and unsaturated fats**, while limiting sugary drinks, heavy alcohol use, and highly processed foods.

That said, **one meal won’t make or break your health**. Overall patterns matter more than perfection.
